defect.rationale: The transaction-wide timeout is measured from each step's start instead of the transaction start. The identity-transformation baseline cannot advance time between steps, so the violation is unreachable without the time.advance operator, which makes this defect a clean discriminator for the spike.

invariant.catalogChange: The Phase 3 catalog registers a per-invariant applicability predicate. The Phase 2 final-outcome map stays valid for the two Phase 2 invariants and is unchanged.

baseline.universe: every registered positive seed in contracts/v0.3/spec-cases.json executed on the defect artifact, plus the structural rejection of the registered spike seed

operator.note: The schedule.release-order and fault.step-outcome requests compose the registered time.advance so each operator's distinct effect is measured on an applicable executed spec.

twoSidedCheck.defectArtifact: candidate-failure with a preserved violation identity

verdictRule.adopt: The invariant's precondition is unreachable under the identity transformation, witnessed by the recorded structural rejection of the registered spike seed; every executed identity baseline seed produces no violation identity equal to the operator candidate on the defect artifact; and at least one operator arm produces a preserved violation identity on the defect artifact that passes the two-sided check, the per-patch F-to-P check, and five-of-five replay.
verdictRule.retire: No operator arm achieves such a candidate within the registered budgets.

notes: The defect artifact is packed from the pinned revision with only the registered manifest edit applied, through the same packed-consumer path as the clean Phase 1 artifact.
Virtual time is interpreter-owned fake timers inside the evaluator; the host wall-clock budget is unaffected by virtual advances.
